library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Standalone Pulsar bundles its own ZooKeeper + BookKeeper + broker in one JVM, so it starts slower than the rabbitmq/nats images already in this repo — poll readiness (e.g. GET http://localhost:8080/admin/v2/clusters, or attempt to open a producer) with a generous timeout (~90-120s) rather than a fixed sleep, following the waitUntil pattern already used in tests/src/com.rabbitmq.client/amqp-client/0.8.0's ClientPropertiesTest. Start the container with `bin/pulsar standalone --no-functions-worker -nss` (same default Testcontainers' own PulsarContainer module uses) to skip functions-worker and BookKeeper-backed stream storage, which the client doesn't need and which slow startup further. Publish port 6650 for the binary client protocol (serviceUrl pulsar://localhost:6650) and 8080 for the admin REST API. Use a fixed container name and remove any stale container in both @BeforeAll and @AfterAll, matching the existing rabbitmq test's cleanup pattern.
risks: Standalone mode is heavier than the single-process brokers already allow-listed (rabbitmq, nats) — CI timeouts may need to be generous, and this adds real wall-clock cost per test run.

This is advisory: if the remaining dynamic-access classes the generator needs turn out to still be reachable without a live broker, the Docker setup adds cost without benefit — local Gradle/Native Image verification should confirm before committing to it.
